content.overview: Such class or classes of companies as may be prescribed shall be required to appoint an internal auditor, who shall either be a chartered accountant or a cost accountant, or such other professional as may be decided by the Board to conduct internal audit of the functions and activities of the company.
content.glance: Prescribed classes of companies must appoint an internal auditor (CA, cost accountant, or other professional as the Board decides).
content.study:
## Section 138 — Internal audit

**Who must appoint.** Such class or classes of companies as may be prescribed (not every company by the section's own words).

**Who may be internal auditor.** A chartered accountant, a cost accountant, or such other professional as the Board decides.

**Scope.** Internal audit of the functions and activities of the company. The Central Government may prescribe the manner and intervals of internal audit and reporting.

**Not statutory audit.** Internal audit under section 138 is not a substitute for the statutory auditor under section 139.

This note is a focused study aid; the topic remains under source and current-law review.

sections.body: Only prescribed classes must appoint an internal auditor.

hypotheticals.question: Is every company required to have an internal auditor under section 138?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Only such class or classes as may be prescribed.

misconceptions.trap: Treating internal audit as the same as statutory audit under section 139.
misconceptions.correction: Section 138 is internal audit for prescribed classes; section 139 is statutory auditor appointment.
